clue.text: Honour judge entering. court on purpose

indicators.note: the judge's letter goes inside the honour, entering it

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A judge deliberately walks into court to receive a royal honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR shows a stray full stop after 'entering'; the printed page has none. 'on' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is an aim or goal, so it is a synonym of purpose.

clue.text: Brother may swear this dog needs such training

definitions.meaning: a monk, a brother, takes vows of poverty, chastity and submission to superiors
classes teaching a dog to sit and come on command

explanation.definitionFit: Monks vow submission to their order, and dogs are trained to follow commands.

clue.text: Sailor taking up sandwich, one found in crow's nest

parts.note: a jack, or Jack tar, is a sailor

indicators.note: in a down answer the word is taken upwards, read backwards

parts.note: wad is British slang for a sandwich or bun

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a sandwich up to the lookout post on a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' reverses WAD to DAW. The crow's nest is literally a crow's nest, not the masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small member of the crow family, so it is found in a crow's nest.

clue.text: Shortly name two unknowns to give buddy protection

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
x and y are the classic algebraic unknowns
x and y are the classic algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: In brief, name two unknown people who will protect your mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' trims CALL to CAL. 'buddy' is read as bud-dy, belonging to a bud; 'to give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The calyx is the ring of sepals that encloses and protects a flower bud.

clue.text: Progressively narrowing competition for stunner

definitions.meaning: a tournament in which losers drop out each round until one remains
a blow that renders someone unconscious, or a gorgeous person

explanation.definitionFit: A tournament format eliminating losers each round, and a stunning blow or beauty, share this one name.

clue.text: Be unlikely to succeed in bid to dispense with grace

definitions.meaning: an idiom for having no chance at all

definitions.text: in bid to dispense with grace
definitions.meaning: literally, to skip saying grace, the short prayer before a meal

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have no chance, and literally means to go without saying grace.

clue.text: Little creature moving about in shade

definitions.text: Little creature moving about in shade

parts.words: Little creature moving about in shade
parts.note: a small lizard famous for changing its skin colour, its shade, as it moves around

explanation.definitionFit: The chameleon is a small lizard that changes the colour of its skin to match its surroundings.

clue.text: Excel at games, but there's pressure to cut expenditure

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the word, splitting it

parts.note: an outlay is money spent
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A sports club excels, but there is pressure to cut its spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' puts P into OUTLAY; 'but there's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To outplay is to play better than an opponent, excelling at a game.

clue.text: One's nothing to do with this instruction from scorer

definitions.text: One's nothing to do with this instruction from scorer

parts.words: One's nothing to do with this instruction from scorer
parts.note: a musician given this marking in the score has nothing to play; the scorer is a composer, not a cricket official

explanation.definitionFit: Tacet is the Latin direction in a musical score telling a performer to stay silent.

clue.text: Music and drama star, could one say?

parts.note: the word arts, performing as an anagram, rearranges into star

explanation.surface: A celebrity of music and theatre is described as a star.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, with PERFORMING as an anagram signal acting on ARTS, and it gives STAR. 'could one say?' is a link flagging the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Music and drama are the main performing arts, done live before an audience.

clue.text: Fine ten rioting beside former part of prison

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a cell is one room of a prison

indicators.note: the word ten runs riot, its letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Ten prisoners riot next to an old cell block, and are fined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' looks like a description of prisoners, but it is the anagram signal on the word ten; 'beside' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent and fine are both words of high approval, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Old Mexican street-map given to investigator

parts.note: an A-Z is a British street atlas, named for its index running A to Z
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A detective is handed a street map of an ancient Mexican city.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is the standard British book of city street maps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people ruling central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Sign for list of unreadable books

definitions.meaning: an indicator or pointer, something that shows a trend
the Catholic Church's ... of prohibited books, which the faithful were forbidden to read

explanation.definitionFit: An index is an indicating sign, and the Index was the Church's catalogue of banned reading.

clue.text: Pulse felt wrong ancient must shortly be admitted

indicators.note: one piece is let in to sit inside the other
felt set wrong, its letters put in a different order
cut short, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: age-old means very old, ancient

explanation.surface: Someone felt their pulse was wrong and an elderly patient must be admitted to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must' is a link, and 'Pulse' means an edible seed such as a bean, not a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small French kidney bean, and beans are pulses.

clue.text: Prepare with resolution for this party time

definitions.text: Prepare with resolution for this party time

parts.words: Prepare with resolution for this party time
parts.note: people make resolutions for the coming twelve months on the night of celebration that ends December

explanation.definitionFit: The last night of December is a party night when people traditionally make resolutions.

clue.text: Tiny space on part of bagpipe for siren, possibly

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an en is a printer's narrow space, half an em
the chanter is the pipe on which a bagpipe's melody is fingered

explanation.surface: A tiny gap in part of a bagpipe makes it sound like a siren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. A siren of legend charms sailors with song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens of Greek myth lured sailors with song, making a siren one example of a bewitching charmer.

clue.text: Leader absent, votes for right

indicators.note: the word's opening letter is taken away

parts.note: ayes are votes in favour, as in Parliament

explanation.surface: With the leader away, the votes go to the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader absent' drops the A from AYES. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'right!' agrees with someone, just as an affirmative reply does.

clue.text: Lavish entertainment, one of a pair for viewers?

definitions.meaning: a grand public show or display

definitions.text: one of a pair for viewers?
definitions.meaning: a single lens of a pair of glasses, which help people see

explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive show, and spectacles are glasses, so one lens is a spectacle.

clue.text: One barked, even in Bedlam

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters (second, fourth, sixth) of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Even in the madhouse, one creature barked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barked' suggests a dog, but the definition means a thing covered in bark, a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is covered in bark, so it is literally a barked thing; this one is a common deciduous tree.

clue.text: TV channels with new style used values of the centre

parts.note: television channels are among the media
NS stands for New Style, the Gregorian calendar dating

explanation.surface: TV channels adopted a new style.
explanation.walkthrough: N.S. is the standard abbreviation for New Style dating. 'with' and 'used' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics a median is the middle value of an ordered set, a measure of the centre.

clue.text: Creator of sticks found damage to stake of wood around tip

parts.note: to chip is to damage by breaking off a small piece

indicators.note: the stake goes round the tip, enclosing it

parts.note: a pale is a pointed wooden stake, as in a fence
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: A woodworker finds a fence stake damaged around its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticks' is slang for furniture. 'found' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chippendale was the famous eighteenth-century English cabinet-maker, and sticks means furniture.

clue.text: A dealer at first about to push drug was up against it

indicators.note: the first pair of letters goes around the rest
only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: to butt is to push with the head
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dealer first about to push drugs found themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and D around BUTT and E. The definition means literally touched against something, not in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutted means bordered or leaned on, being literally up against something.

clue.text: Plant's natural habitat fixed in hard day out

indicators.note: the habitat is set firmly inside the other letters

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: day put out of order, its letters jumbled

parts.note: a species' range is the area where it naturally lives

explanation.surface: A plant's natural home is set in a hard day outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns DAY into YDA; 'fixed in' puts RANGE into H + YDA. The 's of 'Plant's' is a link ('is').
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a flowering shrub, a garden plant with large heads of blooms.

clue.text: One's savings — nothing in what you'd call cash

indicators.note: the letter for nothing goes inside the other word

parts.note: hard cash is a familiar phrase for coins and notes
O resembles the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone's savings amount to nothing in actual money.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD qualifies cash in the stock phrase 'hard cash'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stored-up stock of money or valuables, someone's savings.

clue.text: In the wrong occupation

parts.note: not a bad job but occupying property one has no right to, as an illegally settled building

explanation.definitionFit: A squat is a building occupied without legal right, an unlawful occupation.

clue.text: Endlessly miserable over bird that's extinct in islands

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece is placed over the second
the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: sad means miserable
the moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct

explanation.surface: Someone is endlessly miserable about an extinct bird once found on islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims SAD to SA. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an island group in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Accommodate oneself in a flat — about time

indicators.note: the word for a flat is turned round

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: Someone settles into a flat, and about time too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses PAD to DAP. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to adjust or accommodate oneself to new conditions.

clue.text: Irate and much exercised with inflammatory complaint

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is irate and very worked up about a painful complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercised' looks like 'upset' but signals rearranging IRATE and MUCH; 'and' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic describes someone suffering from rheumatism, a painful inflammatory condition of joints.

clue.text: Unhappiness as teacher gets new head

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is replaced by another

parts.note: a mistress is a schoolteacher, as in a French mistress

explanation.surface: There is unhappiness when a teacher gets a new headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets new head' swaps the M of MISTRESS for a D. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is anguish or suffering, a synonym for unhappiness.

clue.text: Artificial light may be too expensive for game

definitions.meaning: a wax stick with a wick, burnt for illumination

definitions.text: may be too expensive for game
definitions.meaning: from the proverb 'the game is not worth the ...', meaning the effort costs more than the gain

explanation.definitionFit: A candle gives light, and the proverb says a poor game is not worth one.
